Taken clean: 014 released at b4dc64bb4e72 and the stylesheet had not moved since. Two edits planned — the main-item cell's thumb target, and the sheet grab band the outstanding list records as unowned.

Record sheet's grab band stopped at its own header. That sheet pads its top by --db-space-6, four times the menu sheets, so its bar sits 24px down and a band centred on it ran 2..50px from the sheet's top edge while the header starts at 32. Measured consequence: the band answered every press aimed at the title, and both 44px header actions delivered 26px. The title's rename opens on a double-click, so the second tap never reached it — which is why renaming looked as though tap-to-open had removed it from the phone. Band now runs from the sheet's top edge to the bottom of the handle's own margin box: 35px, 0 stolen, title reachable, both actions 44 of 44, and a real double-tap on the title renames again. Menu sheets keep the shared rule unchanged and were measured at 41px with 0 stolen before and after. The band is an invisible pseudo-element, so this is a hit-testing change only: screenshots of both sheet surfaces are byte-identical with the override on and off.

Main-item cell touch target: tried and reverted, byte-identically. A downward negative-inset pseudo-element to lift the 169x34 cell to the 44px floor is a measured no-op here for two independent reasons — the cell clips its overflow, so the pseudo-element is cut back to the cell box (the last row gained 0px), and in a contiguous table the next row's own area begins exactly where this one's box ends, so there are no dead pixels to reclaim. Only row height reaches 44 and that is a density setting. Reverted rather than shipped, since a rule that measures as a no-op advertises a fix that is not there. Replaced by a check that measures the reach and asserts the property that IS achievable: no press lands on the wrong row.

Four switch repairs, each measured. (2) and (3) together: toggles losing a computed property when moved out of the container 10/10 -> 0/10, each half shown failing again on its own. (4) The switch was reachable at 34x18 under this phase's 28px floor; a coarse-pointer ::after band takes it to 34x28 with the painted box unchanged, so no desktop capture moves.

The reorder button and the row checkbox stopped overlapping. Three rules fought over that button and the touch-floor block won something that was not its business: it opened with display:inline-flex, the same weight as the display:none written for these buttons off a phone and later in the file, so a minimum-size rule decided that a phone-only control renders in every desktop list and gallery row, unstyled. Display removed from the floor block; the floor kept. The column was then re-derived: its own comment read 48 = button 24 + checkbox 16 + gap 8, and both controls have since grown to 28 for the touch floor while the column stayed at 48. 4 + 28 + 4 + 28 = 64, matched in getSelectionColumnWidth's touch branch, with the phone pin 6px -> 4px and the phone button declared at the 28px it has been painting all along. Measured gap between the two controls: desktop -17px -> no button rendered at all, which is what production does since the table creates it only on touch; phone -14px in a 49px cell -> +4px in a 65px cell.

Recaptured and reviewed; the record-detail sheet was opened and read at both themes. One rule changed: the record row label moved from --db-font-md to a new --db-font-base step at 14px. THE STEP IS NEW RATHER THAN A RETUNE OF --db-font-md, and the reason is measured: raising --db-font-md to 14 satisfies both type-scale checks but grows the desktop record panel's inline editor 34.8px -> 36.3px, which reddens the geometry 021 has frozen. One line-height of growth, exactly as the font change predicts, and nothing to do with this label. So the step is additive and --db-font-md still reads 13px for its other consumers. --db-font-base has exactly one consumer. TWO CHECKS WERE MUTUALLY UNSATISFIABLE before this: verify-placement bound the label to --db-font-md while the sheet audit required it on the audited scale, and no label value satisfied both while that token read 13px. The placement check now names --db-font-base; the property it asserts is unchanged and a literal 15px on the label still reds it, observed. verify-placement went 233/236 exit 1 -> 234/236 exit 0, and the KNOWN entry for the off-scale label is deleted because a declared red that now passes is a check that can no longer fail. This rule cannot select them: --db-font-base has one consumer and panels.mjs is the only scenario file referencing db-record-detail-field-label. The header stays at align-items:flex-start, which is the right anchor for a title that WRAPS - centring the row would drag the actions to a two-line title's middle. Centring the title against the flex line fixes only the short case: when the title is the tallest item it already fills the line and the rule is a no-op. Measured before and after on the shipped panel: title box 19px beside 44px actions, centres 13px apart -> 0px apart. Observed red first, and the check that measures it is new in the same change.

Taken for a state this packet's own criterion asks about and nothing measured: 'checked, indeterminate, disabled and focus each produce a measurable difference, per family'. The pass built to answer it found the toggle switch reading byte-identical focused and at rest across background, border, image, shadow and opacity — no focus indicator at all, where the three checkbox families each get one from .db-checkbox:focus-visible.

One rule: .db-toggle-switch:focus-visible, the same outline and ring the checkbox carries, because they are the same control to a reader even though they are different shapes. Watched failing by renaming the selector: the family reads 'focus NO'. THE FINDING ALMOST WENT THE OTHER WAY. The first run reported the switch with no checked, indeterminate or focus state, and the cause was the pass reading a signature in the same tick as the state change while the switch's 0.15s background transition was still running — the other three families change background-image, which has no transition, so only one family lied. Transitions are now disabled for that pass. A theme root, a :checked match and a pseudo-element read all had to be ruled out first, and recording it as a product defect would have been a fabricated bug in a shipped control.

Recaptured and reviewed. A focus ring is a :focus-visible state and no capture holds focus, so no PNG moves for this edit and none did beyond the usual churn — which is itself worth stating rather than presenting an unchanged capture set as sign-off. The state pass is the evidence here, and it is in the tool rather than in a picture. Per-image operator sign-off still owed, as for every prior release.

Taken for this packet's own criterion: 'on phone the action never produces a sub-half-height panel'. The cap had been asserted since 003; the floor never was, and a two-field record measured 189px on an 844px screen.

A MINIMUM rather than a fixed height, so a record with more in it still grows to content and still stops at the 90svh cap beside it; svh rather than vh because that is the unit the cap already uses and the two differ by the mobile browser chrome. Watched failing in BOTH directions: removed, the same record measures 145px; pinned to 100svh it measures 844 against a 760 cap. A floor-only check would have passed the second, which is the opposite defect and the one 003's cap exists to prevent.

Taken to close the header-spill row this phase left open rather than leave it as a deferral: at 320px the toolbar's utilities cluster reaches 10px past the header's content box, and nothing spills at 402, 768 or 1440.

One declaration: flex-wrap: wrap on .db-toolbar. The earlier note called the two fixes opposite directions and that was wrong — wrapping is ADDITIVE. flex-wrap does nothing at any width where the row already fits, so 402 and up are untouched by construction, and at 320 the clusters take a second line instead of overhanging. Letting the cluster shrink was the alternative and does not work: it is flex: 0 0 auto with fixed-size icon children and overflow: visible, so shrinking moves the overflow into the cluster rather than removing it. Measured: header descendants past the header's content box 1 -> 0, and back to 1 with the declaration removed.

Recaptured and reviewed. No capture moves: the census measures at 320px and the capture harness renders at 402 and 1440, where the rule is inert by construction — stated rather than presented as sign-off. It does not settle what the narrowest supported width IS, which is still the operator's call; it makes the surface correct at either answer. Per-image operator sign-off still owed.

Taken for a defect the set-equality check this phase asked for found on its first run: the shipped menu row measures 13px inside an owned menu and inside a filter panel, and 16px inside a record-detail sheet. Same component, same class, three containers, two sizes.

One literal fallback: font-size: var(--db-font-md, 13px) on .db-menu-item.db-menu-item. Type tokens live on the plugin's token roots, so a row in a surface mounted outside them resolved the var to nothing, the declaration was dropped entirely, and the row took whatever the host gives a bare button — measured at 14px on a bare page and 16px in the sheet. The switch's radius carries the same fallback for the same reason. TWO THINGS WORTH RECORDING. The fallback was first added to .db-menu-item and changed nothing, because this doubled-specificity rule already owned the property — a shadowed declaration looks exactly like one that did not work. And the existing check for this ('a menu row lays out identically in any sheet') compares min-height, padding and height, all of which the row declares; the one property it did NOT declare is the one that drifted, which is the whole argument for set equality over a spot check. Measured: 3 containers, 2 signatures -> 1. Red again with the fallback removed.
Recaptured and reviewed. The owned-menu and record-sheet captures were opened and read; the rows carry one type across both. Per-image operator sign-off still owed.

The selection count badge carried aria-live and could never announce: bar.empty() rebuilds every child on each selection change, so the badge was a new element every time and a live region only announces changes made inside an EXISTING region. The attribute stated the intent and the structure prevented it. A persistent region now lives outside the bar and needs a visually-hidden rule.

One rule: a visually-hidden live region for the selection count, clipped rather than display:none or visibility:hidden because both of those take the node out of the accessibility tree and the announcement with it. Measured 1x1, clip-path inset(50%), display block, visibility visible — hidden to the eye and present to a screen reader.
Recaptured; the region is invisible by construction so no capture changed. Nothing to sign off per-image here.
